transport: inherited pipe write fd, O_NONBLOCK; one write per line; no retry or waiting
sequence: 0-based sequence counts attempted events; gaps expose dropped events; no wrapping
child_clock: CLOCK_MONOTONIC nanoseconds in same WSL/Linux clock domain as wrapper
emit_contract: emit only records fixed allocation-free POD; emit.pod* lines are flushed after t4 and outside emit. Core freezes exact fields/units separately; wrapper preserves all four integers without reinterpreting them.
producer_error_contract: Do not block on EAGAIN, EINTR, EPIPE, partial write or invalid fd; do not retry. Keep business semantics. Normal wrapper holds reader until wait4 and drain complete. A producer supporting deliberately closed readers must prevent SIGPIPE for its own event write without changing application-wide SIGPIPE policy; core supplies that proof.
consumer_contract: persist received raw bytes immediately with unbuffered write/flush, without fsync; persist parsed event records with receive monotonic timestamp; retain the received prefix after child kill, without promising power-loss or kernel-crash durability; malformed/truncated/gapped stream remains evidence and is marked incomplete
reaper: fork/exec plus exactly one successful wait4; no Popen or competing wait/waitpid
